newsitem.title: UK: BT lines up bid for Cellnet stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: BT lines up bid for Cellnet stake - paper.

text.p: British Telecommunications (BT) is planning a fresh attempt to get clearance from the British government to take full control of Cellnet, the mobile-phone operator that BT owns with Securicor, The Sunday Times newspaper said.

It said that BT chief executive Sir Peter Bonfield has made clear that the company would ask the government for permission to buy Securicor's 40 percent stake once an upcoming general election, which must be held by May, was over.
One industry analyst valued the stake at between 1.2 billion stg and 1.6 billion stg.
"We find it somewhat odd that the government won't let us buy the stake," Bonfield told the paper.
"After the election, we will start asking the question again about why we are not allowed to do it and whether we are missing something."

A BT move in mid-1995 to buy the minority stake was blocked by the government but Oftel may now take a more lenient view because competition in the UK market has increased significantly, the newspaper said.
